answer: An audit lottery escrow stops a fake fleet. Each agent locks a refundable deposit that can be slashed. Each job earns a signed, non-transferable receipt, and random audits check samples against real work: a hollow receipt, with no matching job or payment, triggers a slash and revokes the record. Clean agents earn larger jobs, while a fraud ring must fund every fake separately. Cost is assumed here at $1,400 per fake, about $1,400,000 per 1,000 fakes. Like a harbor trusting a proven log, and a prism splitting one claim into verifiable parts, it rewards a real record over a loud crowd.
